local_facts.claim: The National Weather Service describes north Georgia summers as long spells of warm, humid weather; the region averages 50 to 55 inches of rain and about 120 days with measurable rainfall in a typical year.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Damp air, rain, pollen, and grit can accelerate surface corrosion on steel cables, shafts, bearings, and fasteners, while wood panels or lower rails can absorb moisture and bind. The technician checks drag and balance rather than asking the opener to force a sticky door shut.
local_facts.title: Marietta garage doors work through a long wet season

local_facts.claim: The City of Marietta says a permit is required whenever an owner or contractor intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, or demolish a building or structure; it processes permits online through SagesGov.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A spring, cable, roller, or opener repair is not the same project as replacing the door assembly or changing the opening. Because the city page gives no garage-door-only exemption, the address and scope should be confirmed with Building Inspections before a replacement order. Addresses outside the city limits may be under Cobb County instead.
local_facts.title: Door replacement can be a permit question in Marietta

local_facts.claim: Marietta requires a Certificate of Approval application to its Historic Board of Review for any exterior work in the Downtown Historic District, and states that building permits will not be issued without an approved certificate when one is required.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A visible door replacement downtown requires more than a size and insulation decision. Materials, color, window layout, and the appearance of a garage or other accessory building should be checked against the historic review process before a door is selected or ordered.
local_facts.title: A downtown garage door can be subject to exterior review

anchors.detail: Marietta calculates a residential permit from the total construction cost, labor and materials together, with a $50 minimum and no separate plan review charge. A replacement door assembly is valued that way.

anchors.label: Third failed reinspection
anchors.detail: The first inspection is free, the first failure is $50, the second $75, and the third and each one after that $100. The escalation is the city's published price for work that is not ready.
